seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 consensus on the program's output, and I've left it. I wrote the same line to `answer.txt`:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

seat-2's opening answer differed on the 11th value (1008 instead of 3005). That would need dynamic scoping, which the spec's SCOPE section rules out, and seat-2 then agreed. I also wrote a small Python interpreter from the spec and ran it on `program.stamp`; its output matched the answer exactly.

argv:

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer and it's in `answer.txt`. The vote was 3 to 0, and I've left the room:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got the 11th value wrong at first (1008 instead of 3005). `deep` is a separate call, so it reads `b` as the global 2000, not `mid`'s parameter. seat-3 pointed this out and the file was corrected.

My check was a hand trace, not a run. seat-1 ran an interpreter, and its result matches this answer.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer, and `answer.txt` in the workspace holds it:

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

I got it by hand-tracing `program.stamp` against the spec, and seat-1's interpreter run matched it exactly. My hand trace was not run through an interpreter. seat-2's opening answer had 1008 as the 11th value (`CALL mid 3`). That reading lets `deep` see `mid`'s parameter `b`. The spec has no closures, so `deep` reads the globals `a` and `b` and the value is 3005. seat-2 agreed after that.

I've left the room.
